correctness.rationale: The actual RESULT.md establishes B_n(0)+B_(n+1)(0)=1 and |deg B_n - deg B_(n+1)|<=1 by binary induction, then applies Sylvester-product and root-evaluation formulas including the correct leading coefficient exponent. The degree-tie sequence u_j=(7*4^j-1)/3 has leading pair (1,j+1), resultant 1; two successive odd transformations yield N_m with resultant m, followed by even and 4v+1 maps producing infinitely many strictly increasing witnesses. I checked the degree-gap/constant-term boundaries and independent exact Sympy Sylvester determinants for 120 initial indices plus 96 explicit/repeated witnesses. This corroborates—not replaces—the full induction. Finite-field common roots are not inferred from integer resultant divisibility when degrees drop.

originality.rationale: Rational coprimality of B_n and B_(n+1) in Ulas–Ulas does not determine its absolute integer resultant: coprime primitive pairs can have arbitrary nonzero resultant. Gawron computes degree patterns, which provide a premise but not the recursion and universal positive spectrum. Schinzel 2016 addresses leading coefficients and is a plausible implicit covering source, but only abstract metadata could be inspected (Oxford VPN disconnected); residual risk is explicitly retained. Resultary searches returned no statement asserting this universal integer-resultant spectrum.
